feedback: The essay provides a strong and detailed overview of your internship experience with the Portland Pickles, clearly articulating your roles, responsibilities, and significant learnings. Your application of the EMPAC framework was particularly insightful and well-structured, demonstrating a deep understanding of the business aspects. However, the essay falls short in two key areas: it completely omits any discussion of 'surprises' encountered during the internship, and it provides only a very general statement regarding 'interview positioning' rather than specific insights on how your learnings would be leveraged in future job interviews. Addressing these gaps would significantly enhance the completeness and impact of your reflection.

detailed_results.feedback: Excellent detail provided for this section. You clearly outlined your roles (social media, merch tent, 50/50 raffle, graphics), the extensive hours worked, and a variety of tasks performed. The inclusion of your achievement in 50/50 raffle sales adds significant value.
citations: The interns would work every single game day, from around noon to 11pm, which totaled to around 220 hours of work.
I was usually either on the social media team or in the merch tent.
I enjoyed working in the merch tent, I learned a lot about sales and how to use a POS, as well as anticipating what customers liked and ordering more merchandise.
Occasionally , I would be put on the 50/50 raffle, where I would have to sell tickets to spectators.
I’m proud to say I set the highest record for 50/50 raffle ticket sales with a whopping $1,200!
I went to the office once to help with making graphics for their food and drink specials of the day, making sure to make the signage very clear and receptive to customers.
I convinced all the interns to wear their cowboy boots and hats to the Wild West Night, which made the overall game experience so much fun for everyone!

detailed_results.feedback: This section was not addressed in the essay. There were no explicit mentions of any surprises encountered during your internship experience, whether positive, negative, or unexpected.

While you made a general statement about the experience being useful for 'future jobs,' you did not specifically elaborate on *how* these learnings would be framed or leveraged in an interview setting. The rubric asks for 'how learnings help in interviews,' which implies a more direct connection and articulation of transferable skills for interview scenarios.
citations: Having a summer of sports business under my belt I think will provide great insight and experience for future jobs, regardless if it's in the sports industry or not.

detailed_results.feedback: This section is exceptionally well-done. You thoroughly addressed each component of EMPAC (Entertainment, Matching and Price, Assortment, Convenience) with specific, insightful observations and examples related to the Portland Pickles. The comparison to the Savannah Bananas for Entertainment was particularly effective.
citations: For Entertainment, the Pickles are similar to the Savannah Bananas baseball team, focusing more on entertaining spectators through special themes, rowdy regulars, and fun food and drinks. By playing into what consumers are looking for (a fun time), they can hone into more unconventional tactics that “Keep Portland Weird.”

For Matching and Price, there really isn’t that much competition surrounding the Pickles, and I do think they inflate their prices for food and merch during the game, which is what most sports teams do for these items, but while keeping their ticket prices very cheap.
For Assortment, I think the Pickles have a wide variety for merch and food, but tend to run out quickly , opting for people to look online or at their stand alone merch store as back ups.

Lastly , for Convenience, the Stadium is located in Southeast Portland, which is a pretty central location for people in the greater Portland area. Like mentioned earlier , prices are very accessible and parking is easy to find.
